title: Freedom and Responsibility
text:
Existentialist philosophers argue that human beings are not born with a fixed essence. Instead, individuals define themselves through the choices they make and the responsibility they accept for them. Sartre famously claimed that existence precedes essence, meaning that we first exist and only afterwards become what we are.

This idea can feel liberating, yet it also produces a kind of anxiety, since no external authority can settle what a life should mean. Critics sometimes dismiss the position as gloomy, but many thinkers regarded it as a call to honesty about freedom. The discomfort, in their view, is the price of taking one's own existence seriously.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what do existentialists argue about human beings?
options: They are born with a fixed essence
They define themselves through their choices
They have no capacity for responsibility
They are shaped only by external authority

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what can the idea of freedom produce?
Why might critics describe existentialism as gloomy?
options: Because it denies that people make any choices
Because it places heavy weight on responsibility and the absence of fixed meaning
Because it claims existence has a fixed purpose

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about the discomfort described in paragraph two?
options: It shows that the philosophy has failed
It is a sign that one is taking one's existence seriously
It proves that external authorities are needed
It can be avoided by accepting fixed essences

a feeling of worry about something uncertain
making someone feel free from constraint

paragraph_translations: Екзистенціалісти стверджують, що людина не народжується з незмінною сутністю. Натомість особа визначає себе через свої вибори та відповідальність, яку бере на себе за них. Сартр стверджував, що існування передує сутності, тобто спочатку ми існуємо і лише потім стаємо тим, ким є.

Ця ідея може звільняти, але вона також породжує певну тривогу, адже жодна зовнішня влада не може визначити, яким має бути життя. Критики інколи називають цю позицію похмурою, проте багато мислителів вважали її закликом до чесності щодо свободи. Дискомфорт, на їхню думку, є ціною серйозного ставлення до власного існування.
